svg.text: Where the partitioning work happens — the six phases of the tick fence
Order is a contract, not a convenience. Two of the five edges below exist because moving the work either way would produce a wrong answer.
The tick — systems run in parallel, reading and writing the database
the scheduler has finished the tick; every system is complete by construction
WriteTickFence — the exclusive window
Prep
what moves
this tick
Detects the entities that crossed a cell boundary since the last fence.
The drift throttle decides how many relocations this tick’s budget can afford.
The repair planner ranks degraded cells and nominates the worst of them.
Migrate
the entity
bytes move
Claims the destination slot, copies the component bytes, releases the source slot.
Index updates and entity-map patches are staged here, not applied.
Each worker sorts its own chunk of the batch; the next phase merges the sorted runs.
a batch of (key, old value, new value), already sorted per worker
IndexMassUpdate
secondary
indexes
One partitioning descent per B+Tree over the whole staged batch.
Workers take contiguous key ranges, each snapped forward to a leaf boundary.
The window lets it drop the latch, the version check and the B-link right-walk.
EntityMapUpdate
where each
entity lives
The same treatment on a different axis: partitioned by bucket range, not key range.
Carries the born / died fold and the orphan rollback, deferred out of Migrate.
Picks the bulk path per tick, on the measured entries per bucket — a small batch has no sharing to exploit.
the died-side fold must land before any bound is recomputed from occupancy
AabbRefresh
bounds and
drift
Recomputes the bound of every cluster written this tick, and only those.
One consolidated slot walk carries the recompute, drift detection and the outlier guard.
Updates the per-cell index; a promoted cell’s writes are buffered and replayed in cluster-id order.
Finalize
bookkeeping
and durability
Frees the clusters migration drained to empty, re-checking occupancy first.
Runs the dormancy sweep and the cell bookkeeping.
Emits the WAL record and publishes the tick’s highest log sequence number.
Scheduler phases give no exclusivity. The fence does.
A phase is an ordering contract, not a barrier: a later phase’s
systems may start while an earlier phase’s are still running. On
real traces that eager dispatch is worth 30 to 50 % of pool use.
The fence is different because it runs after the tick, on the driver
thread. A host with no runtime gets the same window for free.
What the window licenses
No optimistic version check, no write latch, no restart handling,
no B-link right-walk, no epoch guard, plain reads instead of
volatile ones, and plain increments on per-cell counters where
workers own disjoint cells. A degraded structure may be thrown
away and rebuilt rather than repaired in place.
The price is one rule: nothing may mutate the database concurrently with the fence.
